title: agentfs one-shot result
description: The object every agentfs command emits under --format json. kind selects the shape of data; schema, kind, version and exit carry the same meaning in every version of this format.

schema.description: The result format the document declares.

kind.description: The command whose result this is, which selects the shape of data.

version.description: The agentfs build that produced the result.

root.description: The workspace the result describes, absent when the result describes no workspace.

exit.description: The code the process terminates with, carried in the result so a reader of a captured file reaches the verdict the process reached.

data.description: The payload kind selects, absent for a result that carries none.

diagnostics.description: Every finding the command accumulated, an empty array for a run that raised none.

diagnostic.title: agentfs diagnostic
diagnostic.description: One machine-readable finding about one workspace document.

code.description: The finding's permanent identifier, which is what a consumer branches on. A code is retired rather than reused.

severity.description: How serious the finding is. A document carrying an error is not usable as state.

path.description: The workspace-relative path of the document the finding is about, absent for a finding about the workspace itself.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer to the member the finding is about, absent when the finding is about the document as a whole.

line.description: The 1-based line of pointer within the document, absent when the position does not resolve.

column.description: The 1-based column of pointer within the document, absent when the position does not resolve.

message.description: Prose naming the condition, for a person to read. It carries no contract and is reworded without a schema version.

hint.description: Prose naming the edit that resolves the finding. Applying it to the document makes the finding go away.

value.description: The offending value prepared for display: a terminal control sequence is replaced by a visible marker, a rune that reorders or hides the text around it is replaced by a visible stand-in, and the text is abbreviated to the ceiling. It does not reproduce the document's bytes.
